subject: geography
title: Economic Development Adventure: Processes
welcome_lead: Why is the world unequal? And how do countries climb the development ladder?
meta_desc: GCSE Geography development processes — DTM, Rostow stages, causes of uneven development.
final_note: You learned the Demographic Transition Model and key causes of uneven development.

concepts.def: High birth + death — population stable, low
LICs export raw goods, import expensive ones

walkthroughs.body_html:
Stage 1: high birth + death rate (pre-industrial).
Stage 2: deaths fall as health improves — population booms (LICs).
Stage 3: births fall too as women educated, contraception (NEEs).
Stage 4: low and stable (HICs like UK).
Stage 5: deaths > births, population shrinks (Japan, Italy).

Physical: landlocked countries (Chad) struggle to trade. Natural disasters set development back. Tropical disease (malaria) limits productivity.

Historical: colonisation extracted resources and drew arbitrary borders.

Economic: LICs export cheap raw materials, import expensive manufactured goods (trade imbalance).

Health: in LICs ~1 in 13 children die before age 5.

Migration: people leave LICs for HICs.

Conflict: scarce resources drive wars (e.g. water, oil).

International migration: brain drain — skilled workers leave LICs/NEEs.

mcqs.q: At which DTM stage does population BOOM as death rates fall but birth rates remain high?
What is a TRADE IMBALANCE typically experienced by LICs?
options: Exporting raw goods, importing expensive manufactures

numericals.q: How many STAGES does the Demographic Transition Model usually have?
numericals.hint: Five — including the modern decline stage.
